paragraphs: Baker, here's what these two letters teach me. Jesus sees EVERYTHING about His people. To Ephesus He says, "I know your deeds, your labor, and your perseverance" (Revelation 2:2), and to Smyrna, "I know your affliction and your poverty" (Revelation 2:9). Hard work and hard times, none of it goes unnoticed.

Now, Ephesus did a lot right, and Jesus said so. But He also said, "You have abandoned your first love" (Revelation 2:4). I think that's the part to sit with, friend. You can stay busy for Jesus and still drift from Him, and I bet that can sneak up on any of us. The good news is He doesn't leave them there. He tells them to "Repent and perform the deeds you did at first" (Revelation 2:5), so the way back is wide open.

Then there's Smyrna, and what Jesus says to them is almost the opposite. He doesn't promise an easy road. He says, "Do not fear what you are about to suffer," and then, "Be faithful even unto death, and I will give you the crown of life" (Revelation 2:10). Whether you're worn out from working or worn down by hard times, the same Jesus who "died and returned to life" (Revelation 2:8) is the One talking to you, and He promises the tree of life to "the one who overcomes" (Revelation 2:7).
